description: T1: Rare-combination combinational Trojan in 8-bit ALU. Uses bit-level signals from legitimate ALU inputs (A, B, OP) as trigger — not arbitrary magic constants.
taxonomy: Digital, combinationally triggered, rare-condition Hardware Trojan (Trust-Hub classification)

trigger.note: All 7 input bits must match simultaneously. Trigger uses only legitimate ALU signals — no hidden inputs.

payload.action: XOR-flip bit [3] of ALU result (single-bit corruption)
payload.note: Deliberately small payload — single bit — so the analyzer can isolate trigger vs payload structures.

structural_hints.expected_trigger_structure: AND-tree of 7 signals → LUT chain → t1_trigger wire
structural_hints.expected_payload_structure: MUX or XOR on Y[3] output path, gated by t1_trigger
structural_hints.expected_extra_cells: 1-2 LUTs for trigger AND-tree + 1 LUT/MUX for payload
structural_hints.affected_logic_cone: Y[3] has additional fan-in from A[7:5], B[7:5], OP[2]
structural_hints.note: Post-synthesis: trigger AND-tree may be absorbed into existing LUTs or split across multiple. Exact cell names depend on Vivado optimization.

ground_truth_cells.note: Populated AFTER synthesis — exact cell names come from the synthesized netlist, not from assumptions.

benchmark_context.t1_purpose: Prove the pipeline — establish the complete analyzer flow from netlist → detection → analysis
benchmark_context.t2_purpose: Prove robustness — more complex combinational trigger with wider/deeper cone (NOT YET IMPLEMENTED)
benchmark_context.t3_purpose: Prove sequential capability — FFs, state, clock paths (NOT YET IMPLEMENTED)
benchmark_context.sca_note: SCA/timing is a parallel analysis dimension applied to all three, NOT a fourth Trojan
